source.description: The NDR fuzz target converts attacker-controlled PoC bytes after the header into a DATA_BLOB for protocol parsing; this parser/materialization point is the scored source, not the libFuzzer callback itself.
source.value_from: Attacker-controlled PoC bytes are read/parsed as the NDR payload blob.; value `blob`; from `DATA_BLOB blob = data_blob_const(data + HEADER_SIZE,`

sink.description: ASan reports a 1-byte read from a freed heap buffer while dump_data_cb formats bytes from the NDR print path.

root_cause.description: The stack buffer st is passed into generated NDR pull/print logic without being initialized; the patch inserts memset(st, 0, sizeof(st)) immediately before this point to clear stale pointer fields.

tainted_value_origin.description: Generated NDR pull code materializes attacker-controlled protocol fields into the local structure buffer st.

coarse_trace.summary: Builds an NDR DATA_BLOB from attacker-controlled PoC bytes and allocates the per-input talloc context.
Uses stack buffer st for generated NDR unmarshalling without first zero-initializing it.
Generated print code traverses the pulled NDR structure.
Generated print code reaches a DATA_BLOB-like field in the netlogon structure.
The print helper forwards the buffer pointer and length to dump_data_cb.
The callback reads from the stale/freed buffer, matching the ASan crash location.

fine_trace.note: Scored source: the fuzz target reads/parses attacker-controlled bytes into the NDR payload blob after the fixed header.

The local structure storage is declared on the stack. It is relevant state, but the vulnerability root cause is the missing zero-initialization before the NDR pull path, which is represented by the following patch-grounded step.
At this point st remains uninitialized; the developer patch inserts memset(st, '\0', sizeof(st)) immediately before this statement so generated NDR pull/print code starts from a known-zero structure.
The selected generated NDR pull function parses attacker-controlled blob fields into st. Because st was not zeroed, fields not overwritten by the parser can retain stale pointer values.
The generated print function traverses the parsed structure and follows pointer/blob fields derived from st.
Generated nbt print dispatch reaches the NETLOGON_SAM_LOGON_REQUEST union arm observed in the ASan stack.
The generated request printer emits a DATA_BLOB-like field; this is the stack frame immediately above ndr_dump_data in the sanitizer trace.
The NDR dump helper forwards the stale buffer pointer to the byte-dump callback.
ASan free_context shows the talloc-backed allocation was freed when the fuzz target released mem_ctx; the UAF symptom appears when a stale pointer to that storage is later printed.
ASan crash_location reports the 1-byte read from the freed heap buffer here.
